name: control-flow-integrity
context: Agent systems that must execute tool calls in the presence of untrusted content (e.g., web pages, emails, documents) without allowing that content to redirect the control flow. The agent plans the full sequence of tool calls upfront, before any untrusted content enters the context. Once a plan is committed, tool outputs (which may contain injection payloads) cannot influence the choice of actions — they can only provide data to already-selected tools. This is a strict form of control-flow integrity that prevents content-borne instructions from hijacking the execution path.
benefits: Prevents prompt injection from redirecting the agent's action sequence
Separation of planning (clean context) from execution (potentially polluted)
Preserves tool-usefulness while blocking injection-driven redirection
More permissive than dual-llm-quarantine (single model, no doubling)
tradeoffs: Cannot adapt the plan based on intermediate tool outputs
Requires the full task to be decomposable into a static plan
Long plans may become stale if environment changes mid-execution
Less flexible than reactive ReAct-style interleaving
use_cases: Email automation where inbox content is untrusted
Web automation where fetched pages may contain injection payloads
CRM automation processing inbound customer requests
Document processing with content from untrusted sources
avoid_when: Tasks that genuinely require adaptive planning mid-execution
Tasks where tool outputs genuinely inform next steps (no untrusted content)
anti_patterns: Updating the plan based on tool outputs from untrusted sources
Feeding untrusted content back into the planner
No validation that the executed plan matches the committed plan
design_principles: Plan in a clean context before any untrusted content is processed
Once committed, tool outputs provide data — not instructions
Validate plan execution against the committed plan at each step
best_practices: Keep the planner isolated from any untrusted content
Serialize the plan before execution begins and log it for audit
Abort and re-plan only at explicitly defined replan triggers, never on tool output content
references: Beurer-Kellner et al., Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections, 2025 — https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.08837
